Entries.Text: View, edit and check the navigation data of a loaded Demon's Souls or Dark Souls map: the NVM navmesh each MSB navmesh part loads, the MCP rooms (one per part), and the MCG graph whose nodes join the navmeshes at their gate triangles. Start in the Overlay tab, which draws them in the viewport; the editing tabs work on what it draws.
Map {0} has no NVM binder (.nvmbnd), so it has no navigation data to show or edit.
Draw the map's NVM triangles (coloured by their flags), gate and entity triangles, MCP rooms and MCG graph over the map. The tabs' viewport modes act on what it draws.
What the overlay draws. Each flag combination of the triangles gets its own colour, listed under Triangle Flags.
Pick triangles and paint their flags (how the AI treats them). Each paint stroke is one undoable edit.
The entities of the picked triangle's navmesh: sets of triangles that an event script can disable by entity ID. Pick a triangle to choose the navmesh.
The MCG graph the AI uses to plan long routes: nodes on the gate triangles between navmeshes, and edges with a cost between the nodes of one room. Also shows the MCP room of the picked navmesh.
Move NVM vertices with a brush. Committing rebuilds each edited navmesh's box tree, sets its MCP room box and moves the MCG nodes on its gates, as one undoable edit.
Check the map's NVMs, MCP and MCG against the rules the game files follow. Issues that the vanilla files also have are marked as inherited.
Clicks add triangles to the selected entity (or remove them).
Clicking a node connects it to the selected node.
Draw only the picked triangle's navmesh, with its MCP room and MCG edges. The brush only reaches what is drawn.
The triangles, filled, one colour per flag combination.
The edges between two triangles of the same navmesh.
Edges with no triangle on the other side: the navmesh's boundary.
The outline of the triangles flagged GATE, where MCG nodes join one navmesh to the next.
The outline of the triangles listed by an NVM entity. The selected entity's triangles are drawn in white.
The box of each MCP room in the map: its navmesh's bounds, plus a metre above and below.
The MCG nodes used by the map's edges, as crosses. The selected node is drawn larger, in pink.
The map's MCG edges, as lines between their nodes. The selected edge is drawn in pink.
{0} navmesh parts, {1} NVM files in the binder; {2} parts have no file.
MCG: {0} nodes, {1} edges, {2} of this map.
The flag combinations of the drawn triangles, in their overlay colours, and how many triangles have each.
What a click in the viewport does.
While on, a click in the viewport picks the overlay triangle under the cursor instead of selecting map objects.
While on, holding the picking button over the overlay paints the triangles under the cursor with the flags below. Each stroke is one undoable edit.
How painting changes a triangle's flags, and which flags.
Give painted triangles exactly the ticked flags.
Add the ticked flags to painted triangles, keeping their other flags.
Remove the ticked flags from painted triangles, keeping their other flags.
The picked triangle. Tick a flag to edit it (undoable).
DOOR (0x8). A few entity triangles have it.
GATE (0x4000): the triangles where MCG nodes join this navmesh to the next. An MCG edge lists the gate triangles at each of its ends.
The entities of the picked triangle's navmesh.
Pick a triangle to choose its navmesh.
The navmesh's entities. Each lists triangles that an event can disable by its entity ID. Select one to draw and edit it.
Select the entity and draw its triangles in white.
Add an entity with the picked triangle to the navmesh.
The new entity's ID, as used by event scripts.
Add an entity with this ID and the picked triangle, and select it (undoable).
The selected entity's ID and triangles.
The entity's ID. Changes when you leave the field (undoable).
While ticked, clicking a triangle removes it from the entity; otherwise, clicks add triangles to it.
While on, clicking a triangle in this navmesh adds it to the entity (or removes it, if ticked above). Each click is one undoable edit.
Remove the entity from the navmesh (undoable). Its triangles stay.
Select an entity, then click triangles of its navmesh.
Show the overlay to work on the graph.
Select nodes, connect them, and set the MCP room boxes.
While on, clicking near an MCG node in the viewport selects it.
While on, clicking another node adds an edge from the selected node to it, in the room that both nodes' gates are in (or else the picked triangle's room), with their distance as the cost (undoable).
The two nodes share no room in this map. Pick a triangle in the room the edge should be in, then connect again.
Set every MCP room box in this map from its navmesh, as the game does: the part-placed NVM bounds plus the room's height margin (undoable). Vertex edits do this for the rooms they change.
Every room box already fits its navmesh.
No node is selected. Choose Nodes, then click one in the viewport.
The selected node's position (in map space) and the gate triangles it sits on.
The node's position. It moves when you leave the field, and its edges' costs scale with their new length (undoable).
Move the node to the point of the last picked triangle (undoable).
Move the camera to the node.
No edge of this map lists gate triangles for this node.
The node's edges: the node at the other end, the room the edge crosses, and its cost.
Select the node at the other end.
The edge's cost (MCG Unk20). Set when you leave the field (undoable). The game's costs are mostly slightly more than the straight distance between the nodes, which here is {0}.
The MCP room of the picked triangle's navmesh: its box and the rooms it connects to.
Pick a triangle to show its room.
Check the map's NVMs (indices, neighbours, box trees, entities), MCP (rooms, boxes, connections) and MCG (edges, node lists, gates), then compare the issues with the vanilla files in the background.
Rebuild each edited navmesh with its moved vertices (including its box tree), set its MCP room box, and move the MCG nodes on its gates, as one undoable edit. Saving the map writes them.
Also move vertices of the map's other navmeshes under the brush, so gates between navmeshes stay joined.
Committed {0} navmeshes ({1} vertices moved). {2} MCG nodes followed, and {3} room boxes were set.
The map has no NVM binder.
Navmesh part {0} loads model {1}, but the binder has no NVM for it.
Triangle {0} refers to vertices {1}, but the NVM has {2}.
Triangle {0} refers to neighbour {1}, but the NVM has {2} triangles.
Triangle {0} lists {1} as a neighbour, but they don't share that edge's two vertices (a few game files do this).
Triangle {0} lists {1} as a neighbour, but {1} doesn't list {0}.
{0} vertices are outside the NVM's root box.
{0} triangles are in no leaf of the box tree, so the game can't find them.
{0} box tree leaf entries refer to a triangle that doesn't touch the leaf (harmless; a few game files do this).
Entity {0} lists {1} triangles the NVM doesn't have.
The MCP has {0} rooms in this map, but the MSB has {1} navmesh parts. Room r is part r.
MCP room {0} ({1}) doesn't fit its navmesh's bounds. Use Set Room Boxes in the Graph tab to fix it.
MCP room {0} connects to room {1}, which doesn't exist.
MCP room {0} connects to room {1}, but not the other way.
MCG edge {0} joins nodes {1} and {2}, which don't all exist.
The MCG edge between nodes {0} is in MCP room {1}, which doesn't exist.
The MCG's node lists and edges disagree at {0}.
The MCG edge between nodes {0} lists gate triangles that navmesh {1} doesn't have.
MCG node {0} is {1} m from the nearest gate triangle. The game's nodes sit on one.

The map's navmeshes: each MSB navmesh part, the NVM it loads and its MCP room. Generate or Duplicate creates a new one (a new part, NVM and room), and Remove deletes one. For the AI to path into a new navmesh, mark its gates and add MCG nodes on them (Graph tab).
The map's navmesh parts in MSB order (MCP room r is part r), the NVM file each loads, and its triangles and entities. Select one for the actions below.
{0} navmesh parts, {1} NVM files; {2} files no part loads.
Select a navmesh in the list above.
No free navmesh model number is left for this map.
Create a navmesh from the collision parts selected in the viewport: either a new navmesh part (at the map's origin) with its NVM and MCP room, or a new NVM for the selected navmesh.
Select the collision parts to walk on in the viewport. The navmesh is made from their low collision (l####).
Replace the selected navmesh's NVM with the generated one, keeping its part. Its MCP box is set from it, and its MCG edges find their gate triangles again. Otherwise, a new navmesh is created.
Mark gates where it meets other navmeshes
Flag GATE on both sides, on triangles whose open edge lies on another navmesh's open edge, like Mark Gates.

Generate the navmesh in the background from the selected collision (wound to face up, because the older games store collision the other way), then add it as one undoable edit. No links are created, because NVMs have none.
Discard the result of the running generation.
Generating from {0} collision triangles ({1} selected parts had no loaded collision).
The selected parts have no loaded collision ({0} without a file). Turn on collision loading and reload the map.
Generated {0} ({1}.nvm, {2} triangles, {3} gate triangles marked). Save the map to write the new NVM. The Map Editor draws its part once the map is reloaded.
Regenerated the NVM of {0}: {1} triangles, {2} gate triangles marked.
Create a navmesh from the selected one's NVM, on a new part moved by the offset, with its own MCP room.
How far to move the copy's part from the source's (in map space).
Add a navmesh part with a copy of this NVM (gate flags and entities cleared, then gates marked at its new position), named the way the game names them, with an MCP room for it (undoable).
Added {0} ({1}.nvm, {2} triangles, {3} gate triangles marked). Save the map to write the new NVM. The Map Editor draws its part once the map is reloaded.
Flag GATE on both sides where the selected navmesh meets others: the triangles whose open edge lies on another navmesh's open edge. MCG nodes then go on those triangles (Graph tab).
How close (in metres) both ends of two open edges must be to count as the same edge.
Flag GATE on the triangles where this navmesh meets another (undoable). The game also flags some triangles further from the edge; paint those by hand if needed.
{0} shares no unmarked open edge with another navmesh.
Remove the selected navmesh from the map: its MSB part, its MCP room and the MCG edges in it, and its NVM unless another part loads it.
Remove the navmesh part, its room (later rooms move down one) and its edges as one undoable edit. Its MCG nodes stay; remove them in the Graph tab if no other edge uses them.
The part {0} wasn't found in the map.
Add and remove MCG nodes, and join a navmesh's nodes.
Add an MCG node at the picked point and select it (undoable). Place it on a gate triangle between two navmeshes, then use Link Room on each.
Remove the selected node and its edges. Later nodes move down one (undoable).

Join every pair of nodes on the picked navmesh's gate triangles (within 2 m) with an edge in its room, with their distance as the cost, like most of the game's rooms. Also connect its MCP room to every room those nodes reach (undoable).
All of {0}'s nodes are already joined.
